Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: unit test — two-point begin produces zero synthesized mouse events and camera zoom responds monotonically to distance increase (fingers apart → zoom in, matching wheel direction); centroid translation pans; lifting one finger ends the gesture and subsequent movement of the remaining finger does nothing.

Changed: GLWidget now accepts touch (WA_AcceptTouchEvents + a touchEvent override) and routes it through a per-widget TouchState state machine (glwidget_touch_p.h): single-finger -> synthesized scaled mouse events via the shared dispatchMouse helper (same HiDPI scaling as a real mouse); two-finger -> Navigate::zoom (pinch, wheel convention) + Navigate::translate (centroid pan), consumed before tool dispatch; extra fingers blacklisted until lift. No tool, camera, or rendering code changed; a new touchnavigationtest unit suite was added and TouchState was marked A_EXPORT so it links under MSVC.
Evidence: commits 0fe08fee6 + caa94c829 on master; OpenSpec change 14/14 tasks done. Qt6 CI run 42552875573 = success (asan leg + all build configs + Linux tests); Windows MSVC CI run 42562047461 = success (both build-installer jobs, i.e. the touch test compiled, linked, and ran on MSVC). Full ctest 49/49; touchnavigationtest 17/17 under xvfb.
Tests: cmake --build build --parallel then xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure = 49/49 (0 failed); xvfb-run ./build/bin/touchnavigationtest = 17 passed, 1 skipped (runner clamps QT_SCALE_FACTOR so HiDPI dpr scaling is not exercised). CI asan leg and Windows MSVC both green.
Unresolved: Real-device feel (digitizer-level timing, point-id reuse, slop) is unverified on physical hardware; the single touch-slop constant (kTouchSlopLogicalPx in glwidget_touch_p.h) may need tuning from device evidence. The logic of every real-device scenario is covered by headless unit tests.
Next: Run the author's HiDPI touchscreen smoke pass (OpenSpec tasks 5.1/5.2); tune the touch slop constant from device evidence if the tap/stroke feel is off.

Initial task mapping:
- GLLA 1 <- OpenSpec 1: [ ] 1.1 Set `Qt::WA_AcceptTouchEvents` on `GLWidget` (in its constructor/initialization) and add a `touchEvent(QTouchEvent*)` override that is the single touch entry point; without it Qt synthesizes primary-point-only mouse events. — Verify: `git grep -n "WA_AcceptTouchEvents" libavogadro/src/glwidget.cpp` finds the attribute set exactly once, on the widget; `touchEvent` override declared in `glwidget.h` and defined in `glwidget.cpp`.
- GLLA 2 <- OpenSpec 2: [ ] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: the class is a `GLWidget` member; `git grep -n "static.*[Tt]ouch" libavogadro/src/glwidget.*` shows no static touch state; states and blacklist fields exist in the class.
- GLLA 3 <- OpenSpec 3: [ ] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: code review shows one shared scaling/dispatch helper used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer (no duplicated coordinate math); a unit test asserts synthesized event positions equal expected scaled values at `devicePixelRatioF() != 1` (via `QT_SCALE_FACTOR=2` where honored, matching hidpiviewporttest's env pattern).
- GLLA 4 <- OpenSpec 4: [ ] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: unit test — a touch that wobbles < slop and lifts produces zero tool-visible events; a tap produces exactly one press+release pair; a stroke produces press, ≥1 move, release in order.
- GLLA 5 <- OpenSpec 5: [ ] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: unit test — two-point begin produces zero synthesized mouse events and camera zoom responds monotonically to distance increase (fingers apart → zoom in, matching wheel direction); centroid translation pans; lifting one finger ends the gesture and subsequent movement of the remaining finger does nothing.
- GLLA 6 <- OpenSpec 6: [ ] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: unit tests — palm lands mid-stroke → stroke events unaffected; resting finger lifts after stroke end → zero events; third finger present at pair break → gesture ends, camera static, third finger's later lift produces nothing.
- GLLA 7 <- OpenSpec 7: [ ] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: unit test — with the navigate tool active, one-finger drag synthesizes press/moves and the fixture camera orbits; with an editing tool active on a decline path the fallthrough still reaches navigate.
- GLLA 8 <- OpenSpec 8: [ ] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.
- GLLA 9 <- OpenSpec 9: [ ] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot or is listed in the manual device pass with an explicit note; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.
- GLLA 10 <- OpenSpec 10: [ ] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `cmake --build build --parallel` (capped at `-j8`) then `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure`: zero failures; every previously passing test still passes.
- GLLA 11 <- OpenSpec 11: [ ] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary.
- GLLA 12 <- OpenSpec 12: [ ] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — Verify: both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) complete success on a run building this change's HEAD.
- GLLA 13 <- OpenSpec 13: [ ] 5.1 On the author's HiDPI touchscreen device (also resolves the deferred fix-hidpi-viewport-coordinates 4.3 interaction scenarios): verify picking/clicking works at all; one-finger rotate; tap-to-erase (tap deletes clicked atom; undo restores); one-finger lasso; draw-a-bond stroke. Record each as pass/fail with the device, OS, scaling, and GL renderer string. — Verify: author-recorded results in this change's discussion or the session journal; any failure triaged — if mouse-equivalent picking is broken, fix the HiDPI interaction bug first (it blocks touch) before continuing.
- GLLA 14 <- OpenSpec 14: [ ] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. — Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted.

- GLLA 2 <- OpenSpec 2: [ ] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: the class is a `GLWidget` member; `git grep -n "static.*[Tt]ouch" libavogadro/src/glwidget.*` shows no static touch state; states and blacklist fields exist in the class.
- GLLA 3 <- OpenSpec 3: [ ] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: code review shows one shared scaling/dispatch helper used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer (no duplicated coordinate math); a unit test asserts synthesized event positions equal expected scaled values at `devicePixelRatioF() != 1` (via `QT_SCALE_FACTOR=2` where honored, matching hidpiviewporttest's env pattern).
- GLLA 4 <- OpenSpec 4: [ ] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: unit test — a touch that wobbles < slop and lifts produces zero tool-visible events; a tap produces exactly one press+release pair; a stroke produces press, ≥1 move, release in order.
- GLLA 5 <- OpenSpec 5: [ ] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: unit test — two-point begin produces zero synthesized mouse events and camera zoom responds monotonically to distance increase (fingers apart → zoom in, matching wheel direction); centroid translation pans; lifting one finger ends the gesture and subsequent movement of the remaining finger does nothing.
- GLLA 6 <- OpenSpec 6: [ ] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: unit tests — palm lands mid-stroke → stroke events unaffected; resting finger lifts after stroke end → zero events; third finger present at pair break → gesture ends, camera static, third finger's later lift produces nothing.
- GLLA 7 <- OpenSpec 7: [ ] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: unit test — with the navigate tool active, one-finger drag synthesizes press/moves and the fixture camera orbits; with an editing tool active on a decline path the fallthrough still reaches navigate.

- GLLA 2 <- OpenSpec 2: [ ] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: the class is a `GLWidget` member; `git grep -n "static.*[Tt]ouch" libavogadro/src/glwidget.*` shows no static touch state; states and blacklist fields exist in the class.
- GLLA 3 <- OpenSpec 3: [ ] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). - GLLA 4 <- OpenSpec 4: [ ] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: unit test — a touch that wobbles < slop and lifts produces zero tool-visible events; a tap produces exactly one press+release pair; a stroke produces press, ≥1 move, release in order.
- GLLA 5 <- OpenSpec 5: [ ] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: unit test — two-point begin produces zero synthesized mouse events and camera zoom responds monotonically to distance increase (fingers apart → zoom in, matching wheel direction); centroid translation pans; lifting one finger ends the gesture and subsequent movement of the remaining finger does nothing.
- GLLA 6 <- OpenSpec 6: [ ] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: unit tests — palm lands mid-stroke → stroke events unaffected; resting finger lifts after stroke end → zero events; third finger present at pair break → gesture ends, camera static, third finger's later lift produces nothing.
- GLLA 7 <- OpenSpec 7: [ ] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: unit test — with the navigate tool active, one-finger drag synthesizes press/moves and the fixture camera orbits; with an editing tool active on a decline path the fallthrough still reaches navigate.

Initial task mapping:
- GLLA 1 <- OpenSpec 1: [ ] 1.1 Set `Qt::WA_AcceptTouchEvents` on `GLWidget` (in its constructor/initialization) and add a `touchEvent(QTouchEvent*)` override that is the single touch entry point; without it Qt synthesizes primary-point-only mouse events. — Verify: `git grep -n "WA_AcceptTouchEvents" libavogadro/src/glwidget.cpp` finds the attribute set exactly once, on the widget; `touchEvent` override declared in `glwidget.h` and defined in `glwidget.cpp`.
- GLLA 2 <- OpenSpec 2: [ ] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: the class is a `GLWidget` member; `git grep -n "static.*[Tt]ouch" libavogadro/src/glwidget.*` shows no static touch state; states and blacklist fields exist in the class.
- GLLA 3 <- OpenSpec 3: [ ] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: code review shows one shared scaling/dispatch helper used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer (no duplicated coordinate math); a unit test asserts synthesized event positions equal expected scaled values at `devicePixelRatioF() != 1` (via `QT_SCALE_FACTOR=2` where honored, matching hidpiviewporttest's env pattern).
- GLLA 4 <- OpenSpec 4: [ ] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: unit test — a touch that wobbles < slop and lifts produces zero tool-visible events; a tap produces exactly one press+release pair; a stroke produces press, ≥1 move, release in order.
- GLLA 5 <- OpenSpec 5: [ ] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: unit test — two-point begin produces zero synthesized mouse events and camera zoom responds monotonically to distance increase (fingers apart → zoom in, matching wheel direction); centroid translation pans; lifting one finger ends the gesture and subsequent movement of the remaining finger does nothing.
- GLLA 6 <- OpenSpec 6: [ ] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: unit tests — palm lands mid-stroke → stroke events unaffected; resting finger lifts after stroke end → zero events; third finger present at pair break → gesture ends, camera static, third finger's later lift produces nothing.
- GLLA 7 <- OpenSpec 7: [ ] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: unit test — with the navigate tool active, one-finger drag synthesizes press/moves and the fixture camera orbits; with an editing tool active on a decline path the fallthrough still reaches navigate.
- GLLA 8 <- OpenSpec 8: [ ] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.
- GLLA 9 <- OpenSpec 9: [ ] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot or is listed in the manual device pass with an explicit note; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.
- GLLA 10 <- OpenSpec 10: [ ] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `cmake --build build --parallel` (capped at `-j8`) then `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure`: zero failures; every previously passing test still passes.
- GLLA 11 <- OpenSpec 11: [ ] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary.
- GLLA 12 <- OpenSpec 12: [ ] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — Verify: both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) complete success on a run building this change's HEAD.
- GLLA 13 <- OpenSpec 13: [ ] 5.1 On the author's HiDPI touchscreen device (also resolves the deferred fix-hidpi-viewport-coordinates 4.3 interaction scenarios): verify picking/clicking works at all; one-finger rotate; tap-to-erase (tap deletes clicked atom; undo restores); one-finger lasso; draw-a-bond stroke. Record each as pass/fail with the device, OS, scaling, and GL renderer string. — Verify: author-recorded results in this change's discussion or the session journal; any failure triaged — if mouse-equivalent picking is broken, fix the HiDPI interaction bug first (it blocks touch) before continuing.
- GLLA 14 <- OpenSpec 14: [ ] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. — Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

findingGroups.title: Single-finger touch synthesis
findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as scaled mouse events through the shared dispatchMouse helper (no separate touch coordinate path), so HiDPI picking/stroke/lasso agree with the rendered frame. — glwidget.cpp touchEvent -> TouchState -> dispatchMouse; touchnavigationtest testTapErasesAtom, testLassoThroughSynthesis, testMouseRegressionGuard pass.

Jitter below the ~10 logical-px slop is swallowed; a quick release below slop synthesizes a press+release click; travel >= slop synthesizes press then moves. — TouchState PENDING->STROKE/tap; testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke, testTapSynthesizesClick, testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease pass.

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures
findings: Two-finger pinch zooms (Navigate::zoom, wheel convention: fingers apart = zoom in) and centroid movement pans (Navigate::translate), consumed before any tool sees input. — testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut, testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid pass; gesture ends when either original finger lifts and holds the camera (testGestureEndHoldsCamera).

findingGroups.title: Extra fingers / palm rejection
findings: Any point arriving while a stroke/pending/gesture is in flight is blacklisted until lift, and never promoted; the blacklist survives stroke end so a resting finger never wakes; a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair. — testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted, testRestingFingerNeverWakes, testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch pass.

findingGroups.title: Single-finger touch synthesis
findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as scaled mouse events through the shared dispatchMouse helper (no separate touch coordinate path), so HiDPI picking/stroke/lasso agree with the rendered frame. — glwidget.cpp touchEvent -> TouchState -> dispatchMouse; touchnavigationtest testTapErasesAtom, testLassoThroughSynthesis, testMouseRegressionGuard pass.

Jitter below the ~10 logical-px slop is swallowed; a quick release below slop synthesizes a press+release click; travel >= slop synthesizes press then moves. — TouchState PENDING->STROKE/tap; testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke, testTapSynthesizesClick, testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease pass.

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures
findings: Two-finger pinch zooms (Navigate::zoom, wheel convention: fingers apart = zoom in) and centroid movement pans (Navigate::translate), consumed before any tool sees input. — testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut, testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid pass; gesture ends when either original finger lifts and holds the camera (testGestureEndHoldsCamera).

findingGroups.title: Extra fingers / palm rejection
findings: Any point arriving while a stroke/pending/gesture is in flight is blacklisted until lift, and never promoted; the blacklist survives stroke end so a resting finger never wakes; a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair. — testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted, testRestingFingerNeverWakes, testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch pass.

findings: Single-finger touch reaches tools as scaled mouse events through the shared dispatchMouse helper (no separate touch coordinate path), so HiDPI picking/stroke/lasso agree with the rendered frame. — glwidget.cpp touchEvent -> TouchState -> dispatchMouse; touchnavigationtest testTapErasesAtom, testLassoThroughSynthesis, testMouseRegressionGuard pass.

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures
findings: Two-finger pinch zooms (Navigate::zoom, wheel convention: fingers apart = zoom in) and centroid movement pans (Navigate::translate), consumed before any tool sees input. — testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut, testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid pass; gesture ends when either original finger lifts and holds the camera (testGestureEndHoldsCamera).

findings: Any point arriving while a stroke/pending/gesture is in flight is blacklisted until lift, and never promoted; the blacklist survives stroke end so a resting finger never wakes; a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair. — testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted, testRestingFingerNeverWakes, testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch pass.

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

findingGroups.title: Two-finger camera gestures

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Set `Qt::WA_AcceptTouchEvents` on `GLWidget` (in its constructor/initialization) and add a `touchEvent(QTouchEvent*)` override that is the single touch entry point; without it Qt synthesizes primary-point-only mouse events. — Verify: `WA_AcceptTouchEvents` set exactly once (glwidget.cpp:822); `touchEvent` declared in glwidget.h:683 and defined in glwidget.cpp:3270.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: one shared `dispatchMouse` helper (glwidget.cpp:3159) used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer; `testSynthesizedPositionScalesWithDpr` asserts scaled positions (skips where QT_SCALE_FACTOR is not honored, mirroring hidpiviewporttest).

[OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.
[OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed, 0 failed.

[OpenSpec 11] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary. — **Verified**: run 42552875573 (commit 0fe08fe) = success; asan (autooptrepro) + all 4 build configs passed.

[OpenSpec 12] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — **Verified**: run 42562047461 (commit caa94c8) = success; both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed. The `touchnavigationtest` compiled AND linked AND ran green on MSVC. (Initial attempt failed with LNK2019 `TouchState::process` unresolved: the method was out-of-line in glwidget.cpp with no `A_EXPORT`, so MSVC did not dllexport it from avogadro.dll. Marking `detail::TouchState` `A_EXPORT` fixed it — dlexport on Windows, `visibility("default")` no-op on Linux.) — **Deferred (external)**: needs a push to remote + `gh workflow run`; local build passes.

[OpenSpec 13] 5.1 On the author's HiDPI touchscreen device (also resolves the deferred fix-hidpi-viewport-coordinates 4.3 interaction scenarios): verify picking/clicking works at all; one-finger rotate; tap-to-erase (tap deletes clicked atom; undo restores); one-finger lasso; draw-a-bond stroke. Record each as pass/fail with the device, OS, scaling, and GL renderer string. - Verify: author-recorded results in this change's discussion or the session journal; any failure triaged - if mouse-equivalent picking is broken, fix the HiDPI interaction bug first (it blocks touch) before continuing. — **Device pass started (author hardware)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen). Observed: one-finger rotate with the navigate tool **passes**. Picking/clicking, tap-to-erase, one-finger lasso, draw-a-bond: not yet recorded. Windows build, display scaling, and GL renderer string: not yet captured.

[OpenSpec 14] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. - Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted. — **Device result (partial)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen): pinch zoom **FAILS** — two fingers never zoom the camera (observed with the navigate tool active; the gesture is tool-independent by design, so the failure is in gesture formation, not tool dispatch). Diagnosis pending on-device discrimination — see 5.3 (the grouping hypothesis was refuted against Qt 6.6 primary sources). Remaining scenarios (two-finger pan, mixed pinch-and-drag, gesture-end camera hold, palm-while-stroke, resting-finger, both-fingers-begin, zoom/pan during AutoOpt): not yet recorded.

[OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

[OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition() (window-local), but on a child widget Qt maps position() to the receiving widget while scenePosition stays window-local (QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the canvas's window offset (toolbar/dock chrome); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level. Use position() in posOf() and pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget. (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. [OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. [OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.

(c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: one shared `dispatchMouse` helper (glwidget.cpp:3159) used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer; `testSynthesizedPositionScalesWithDpr` asserts scaled positions (skips where QT_SCALE_FACTOR is not honored, mirroring hidpiviewporttest).

[OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.
[OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed, 0 failed.

[OpenSpec 11] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary. — **Verified**: run 42552875573 (commit 0fe08fe) = success; asan (autooptrepro) + all 4 build configs passed.

[OpenSpec 12] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — **Verified**: run 42562047461 (commit caa94c8) = success; both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed. The `touchnavigationtest` compiled AND linked AND ran green on MSVC. (Initial attempt failed with LNK2019 `TouchState::process` unresolved: the method was out-of-line in glwidget.cpp with no `A_EXPORT`, so MSVC did not dllexport it from avogadro.dll. Marking `detail::TouchState` `A_EXPORT` fixed it — dlexport on Windows, `visibility("default")` no-op on Linux.) — **Deferred (external)**: needs a push to remote + `gh workflow run`; local build passes.

[OpenSpec 13] 5.1 On the author's HiDPI touchscreen device (also resolves the deferred fix-hidpi-viewport-coordinates 4.3 interaction scenarios): verify picking/clicking works at all; one-finger rotate; tap-to-erase (tap deletes clicked atom; undo restores); one-finger lasso; draw-a-bond stroke. Record each as pass/fail with the device, OS, scaling, and GL renderer string. - Verify: author-recorded results in this change's discussion or the session journal; any failure triaged - if mouse-equivalent picking is broken, fix the HiDPI interaction bug first (it blocks touch) before continuing. — **Device pass started (author hardware)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen). Observed: one-finger rotate with the navigate tool **passes**. Picking/clicking, tap-to-erase, one-finger lasso, draw-a-bond: not yet recorded. Windows build, display scaling, and GL renderer string: not yet captured.

[OpenSpec 14] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. - Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted. — **Device result (partial)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen): pinch zoom **FAILS** — two fingers never zoom the camera (observed with the navigate tool active; the gesture is tool-independent by design, so the failure is in gesture formation, not tool dispatch). Diagnosis pending on-device discrimination — see 5.3 (the grouping hypothesis was refuted against Qt 6.6 primary sources). Remaining scenarios (two-finger pan, mixed pinch-and-drag, gesture-end camera hold, palm-while-stroke, resting-finger, both-fingers-begin, zoom/pan during AutoOpt): not yet recorded.

[OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

[OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition() (window-local), but on a child widget Qt maps position() to the receiving widget while scenePosition stays window-local (QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the canvas's window offset (toolbar/dock chrome); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level. Use position() in posOf() and pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget. (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.

- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. [OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. [OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.

(c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: one shared `dispatchMouse` helper (glwidget.cpp:3159) used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer; `testSynthesizedPositionScalesWithDpr` asserts scaled positions (skips where QT_SCALE_FACTOR is not honored, mirroring hidpiviewporttest).

[OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.
[OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed, 0 failed.

[OpenSpec 11] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary. — **Verified**: run 42552875573 (commit 0fe08fe) = success; asan (autooptrepro) + all 4 build configs passed.

[OpenSpec 12] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — **Verified**: run 42562047461 (commit caa94c8) = success; both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed. The `touchnavigationtest` compiled AND linked AND ran green on MSVC. (Initial attempt failed with LNK2019 `TouchState::process` unresolved: the method was out-of-line in glwidget.cpp with no `A_EXPORT`, so MSVC did not dllexport it from avogadro.dll. Marking `detail::TouchState` `A_EXPORT` fixed it — dlexport on Windows, `visibility("default")` no-op on Linux.) — **Deferred (external)**: needs a push to remote + `gh workflow run`; local build passes.

[OpenSpec 13] 5.1 On the author's HiDPI touchscreen device (also resolves the deferred fix-hidpi-viewport-coordinates 4.3 interaction scenarios): verify picking/clicking works at all; one-finger rotate; tap-to-erase (tap deletes clicked atom; undo restores); one-finger lasso; draw-a-bond stroke. Record each as pass/fail with the device, OS, scaling, and GL renderer string. - Verify: author-recorded results in this change's discussion or the session journal; any failure triaged - if mouse-equivalent picking is broken, fix the HiDPI interaction bug first (it blocks touch) before continuing. — **Device pass started (author hardware)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen). Observed: one-finger rotate with the navigate tool **passes**. Picking/clicking, tap-to-erase, one-finger lasso, draw-a-bond: not yet recorded. Windows build, display scaling, and GL renderer string: not yet captured.

[OpenSpec 14] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. - Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted. — **Device result (partial)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen): pinch zoom **FAILS** — two fingers never zoom the camera (observed with the navigate tool active; the gesture is tool-independent by design, so the failure is in gesture formation, not tool dispatch). Diagnosis pending on-device discrimination — see 5.3 (the grouping hypothesis was refuted against Qt 6.6 primary sources). Remaining scenarios (two-finger pan, mixed pinch-and-drag, gesture-end camera hold, palm-while-stroke, resting-finger, both-fingers-begin, zoom/pan during AutoOpt): not yet recorded.

[OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

[OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition() (window-local), but on a child widget Qt maps position() to the receiving widget while scenePosition stays window-local (QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the canvas's window offset (toolbar/dock chrome); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level. Use position() in posOf() and pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget. (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.

- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.
