- GLLA 15 <- OpenSpec 15: [ ] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.
- GLLA 16 <- OpenSpec 16: [ ] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition() (window-local), but on a child widget Qt maps position() to the receiving widget while scenePosition stays window-local (QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the canvas's window offset (toolbar/dock chrome); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level. Use position() in posOf() and pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget. (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.
goal.verificationContract:
1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

2. Every explicit requirement and scenario in the active OpenSpec change has corresponding implementation evidence.

3. OpenSpec task completion accurately reflects the actual codebase state; no checkbox is marked complete merely because work was attempted.

4. Relevant builds, tests, and regression checks pass.

5. No known required work, implementation blocker, knowingly failing relevant test, or silently deferred required task remains.

6. A final comparison of the OpenSpec artifacts against the resulting implementation finds no substantive omission.

7. The repository is left in a coherent state suitable for subsequent OpenSpec verification/archive work.

8. Every mirrored GLLA task is complete (the GLLA task list shows no open tasks), so GLLA's pending-task gate does not refuse completion.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

[OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition() (window-local), but on a child widget Qt maps position() to the receiving widget while scenePosition stays window-local (QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the canvas's window offset (toolbar/dock chrome); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level. Use position() in posOf() and pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget. (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition() (window-local), but on a child widget Qt maps position() to the receiving widget while scenePosition stays window-local (QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the canvas's window offset (toolbar/dock chrome); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level. Use position() in posOf() and pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget. (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. [OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. tasks.title: [OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is already refuted against Qt 6.6 primary sources; the ranked-causes discrimination protocol is fully documented in the change's design/tasks, and the code-side correctness fixes it enabled (5.4) are implemented, tested…

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition() (window-local), but on a child widget Qt maps position() to the receiving widget while scenePosition stays window-local (QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the canvas's window offset (toolbar/dock chrome); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level. Use position() in posOf() and pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget. (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Do not declare the GLLA goal complete based only on previous conversation claims or task checkboxes. Verify against current repository and OpenSpec evidence.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). [OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). [OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed, 0 failed.

[OpenSpec 11] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary. — **Verified**: run 42552875573 (commit 0fe08fe) = success; asan (autooptrepro) + all 4 build configs passed.

[OpenSpec 12] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — **Verified**: run 42562047461 (commit caa94c8) = success; both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed. [OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

Windows build, display scaling, and GL renderer string: not yet captured.

[OpenSpec 14] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. - Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted. — **Device result (partial)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen): pinch zoom **FAILS** — two fingers never zoom the camera (observed with the navigate tool active; the gesture is tool-independent by design, so the failure is in gesture formation, not tool dispatch). Diagnosis pending on-device discrimination — see 5.3 (the grouping hypothesis was refuted against Qt 6.6 primary sources). Remaining scenarios (two-finger pan, mixed pinch-and-drag, gesture-end camera hold, palm-while-stroke, resting-finger, both-fingers-begin, zoom/pan during AutoOpt): not yet recorded.

[OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

[OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 22 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed; the boundary-correction mechanism (mapToGlobal, over position()-in-posOf() because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only) was validated against Qt 6.4.2 primary sources — scenePosition() == globalPosition(), and updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal — and the discriminating test (parent moved to a non-zero global position) fails on the old mapTo(window) offset and passes on mapToGlobal.

tasks.title: [OpenSpec 1] 1.1 Set `Qt::WA_AcceptTouchEvents` on `GLWidget` (in its constructor/initialization) and add a `touchEvent(QTouchEvent*)` override that is the single touch entry point; without it Qt synthesizes primary-point-only mouse events. — Verify: `WA_AcceptTouchEvents` set exactly once (glwidget.cpp:822); `touchEvent` declared in glwidget.h:683 and defined in glwidget.cpp:3270.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: one shared `dispatchMouse` helper (glwidget.cpp:3159) used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer; `testSynthesizedPositionScalesWithDpr` asserts scaled positions (skips where QT_SCALE_FACTOR is not honored, mirroring hidpiviewporttest).

[OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.

[OpenSpec 9] 3.2 Cover the spec scenarios in tests where headless-verifiable: tap click parity (atom deleted via erase tap / element change via draw tap), lasso through synthesis, jitter swallow, two-finger zoom/pan and gesture-end camera hold, blacklist survival, pair break, both-fingers-begin, mouse regression guard (existing mouse-event paths unchanged). — Verify: each spec scenario maps to a named test slot; `xvfb-run ctest -R "touchnavigationtest|erasetooltest|drawtooltest" --output-on-failure` passes.
[OpenSpec 10] 3.3 Full-suite regression: touch pipeline must not alter mouse/wheel/keyboard behavior. — Verify: `xvfb-run ctest --output-on-failure` = 49/49 passed, 0 failed.

[OpenSpec 11] 4.1 Qt6 CI green on the change branch (Linux build + tests, including the asan leg for the new touch code paths). — Verify: Qt6 CI workflow run on the branch completes success; asan job passes with the new test binary. — **Verified**: run 42552875573 (commit 0fe08fe) = success; asan (autooptrepro) + all 4 build configs passed.

[OpenSpec 12] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — **Verified**: run 42562047461 (commit caa94c8) = success; both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed. The `touchnavigationtest` compiled AND linked AND ran green on MSVC. [OpenSpec 13] 5.1 On the author's HiDPI touchscreen device (also resolves the deferred fix-hidpi-viewport-coordinates 4.3 interaction scenarios): verify picking/clicking works at all; one-finger rotate; tap-to-erase (tap deletes clicked atom; undo restores); one-finger lasso; draw-a-bond stroke. Record each as pass/fail with the device, OS, scaling, and GL renderer string. - Verify: author-recorded results in this change's discussion or the session journal; any failure triaged - if mouse-equivalent picking is broken, fix the HiDPI interaction bug first (it blocks touch) before continuing. — **Device pass started (author hardware)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen). Observed: one-finger rotate with the navigate tool **passes**. Picking/clicking, tap-to-erase, one-finger lasso, draw-a-bond: not yet recorded. Windows build, display scaling, and GL renderer string: not yet captured.

[OpenSpec 14] 5.2 Touch-specific checks on the same device: pinch zoom direction and smoothness (no camera jumps); two-finger pan; mixed pinch-and-drag; gesture end holds the camera; palm-while-stroke rejection; resting-finger-never-wakes; both-fingers-at-once starts a gesture; zoom/pan while an auto-optimization session ticks shows no blank frames. - Verify: author-recorded results; any behavioral gap filed as a follow-up change rather than silently accepted. — **Device result (partial)**: ThinkPad P52 (Windows, touchscreen): pinch zoom **FAILS** — two fingers never zoom the camera (observed with the navigate tool active; the gesture is tool-independent by design, so the failure is in gesture formation, not tool dispatch). Diagnosis pending on-device discrimination — see 5.3 (the grouping hypothesis was refuted against Qt 6.6 primary sources). Remaining scenarios (two-finger pan, mixed pinch-and-drag, gesture-end camera hold, palm-while-stroke, resting-finger, both-fingers-begin, zoom/pan during AutoOpt): not yet recorded.

[OpenSpec 15] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool.

[OpenSpec 16] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 22 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed; the boundary-correction mechanism (mapToGlobal, over position()-in-posOf() because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only) was validated against Qt 6.4.2 primary sources — scenePosition() == globalPosition(), and updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal — and the discriminating test (parent moved to a non-zero global position) fails on the old mapTo(window) offset and passes on mapToGlobal.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

[OpenSpec 3] 1.3 Synthesized `QMouseEvent`s are built with widget-local logical positions from `QEventPoint` and routed through the existing `devicePixelRatioF()` scaled-event construction and the tool → navigate-fallback dispatch (identical to the real mouse handlers). [OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

[OpenSpec 8] 3.1 Add `libavogadro/tests/touchnavigationtest.cpp` + CMakeLists entry, modeled on the hidpiviewporttest/erasetooltest fixture pattern (offscreen `GLWidget`, molecule fixture, direct event injection — no real touch stack needed). Drive the state machine with constructed `QTouchEvent` sequences carrying explicit point ids/positions/timestamps. — Verify: `cmake --build build --target touchnavigationtest -j8` succeeds; `xvfb-run ctest -R touchnavigationtest --output-on-failure` passes; skip paths mirror hidpiviewporttest where `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is not honored.

[OpenSpec 12] 4.2 Windows/MSVC: trigger the Windows installer workflow after Linux CI passes (`gh workflow run 168745168 --ref <branch> --repo thosoo/avogadro`) — new code must compile under `-std:c++17 -permissive-` (D8: explicit constructors, Qt 6.4 `QEventPoint` APIs, no aggregate-init pitfalls). — **Verified**: run 42562047461 (commit caa94c8) = success; both `build-installer` jobs (installer + tests) passed. At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

- the current OpenSpec status;

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

[OpenSpec 2] 1.2 Add a per-widget touch state machine class (internal to glwidget.cpp or a small paired header) with states `IDLE/PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE`, point-id tracking, and the second-class blacklist; it consumes touch point lists and emits synthesized mouse events plus camera deltas. No static/global state (D6). — Verify: `detail::TouchState m_touch` is a GLWidget member (glwidget.cpp:385); `git grep static.*[Tt]ouch glwidget.*` is empty; states + `m_blacklist`/`m_primaryId` in glwidget_touch_p.h:112,165,181.

The click pair's press and release share a timestamp. — Verify: one shared `dispatchMouse` helper (glwidget.cpp:3159) used by both mouse handlers and the synthesizer; `testSynthesizedPositionScalesWithDpr` asserts scaled positions (skips where QT_SCALE_FACTOR is not honored, mirroring hidpiviewporttest).

[OpenSpec 4] 2.1 Implement PENDING → STROKE: travel ≥ slop (named constant, ~10 logical px) synthesizes press at current position then moves; implement tap: release < slop and quick synthesizes press+release pair; jitter below slop emits nothing. — Verify: `testJitterBelowSlopEmitsNothingThenStroke`, `testTapSynthesizesClick`, `testStrokeSynthesizesPressMoveRelease`.

[OpenSpec 5] 2.2 Implement GESTURE: entered when a second point is observed while PENDING *or* a `TouchBegin` carries ≥2 points (straight to GESTURE, no pending state, no synthesized tool events); distance delta between the two tracked point ids drives `Navigate::zoom` with the wheel sign convention (fingers apart = zoom in); centroid delta drives `Navigate::translate` pan; the gesture ends when either original point id lifts, leaving the camera at its final pose; neither gesture's zoom nor pan reaches any tool. — Verify: `testBothFingersBeginGoesStraightToGesture`, `testPinchSpreadZoomsInAndSqueezeZoomsOut`, `testTwoFingerPanMovesCentroid`, `testGestureEndHoldsCamera`, `testSecondPointDuringPendingBecomesGesture`.

[OpenSpec 6] 2.3 Implement the second-class rule: any point arriving during PENDING/STROKE/GESTURE is blacklisted until it lifts; the blacklist survives stroke end (a resting finger that lifts after a stroke never becomes a fresh touch); a third finger never substitutes into a broken pinch pair; STROKE completion on finger-1's release still synthesizes the release normally while finger-2 stays blacklisted. — Verify: `testPalmMidStrokeIsBlacklisted`, `testRestingFingerNeverWakes`, `testThirdFingerDoesNotSubstituteIntoPinch`.

[OpenSpec 7] 2.4 Preserve one-finger rotate: a synthesized press the active tool ignores falls through to `m_navigateTool` exactly as a real mouse press does. — Verify: `testOneFingerRotateWithNavigateTool`.

Shares the release-synthesis mechanics already decided for cancel-mid-stroke (D9/Risks); respects the verified DrawTool mechanics (press mutates the live molecule directly, drawtool.cpp:291–296; the undo command exists only at release, drawtool.cpp:607–615). [OpenSpec 16] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Protocol — step 0: verify the installed binary is a build of master ≥ caa94c829 (fresh artifact from Windows CI run 42562047461 or later); step 1: `set QT_LOGGING_RULES=qt.qpa.events.debug=true` then `avogadro.exe -platform windows:verbose=2 > touch-trace.log 2>&1`, pinch in 2–3 styles (normal; careful-plant-then-spread; simultaneous land). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool. — **Discriminated (device evidence, no trace needed)**: the fresh P52 report (run 42630304893 installer, P0-fixed binary) shows the symptom **draws an atom immediately** with the draw tool active — the press demonstrably reaches the tool, so cause (1) is ruled out, and the symptom is exactly cause (2) (finger 1 crosses slop → STROKE → press → draw tool creates an atom; finger 2 arrives and is blacklisted → no zoom). The evidence-backed fix (task 5.5, stroke-arming grace window) is implemented and unit-verified (touchnavigationtest 26 passed / 1 skipped, full ctest 49/49); causes (3)/(4) are not implicated by the observed symptom and are not re-investigated. On-device re-record of the fixed pinch (5.2) remains on the author's hardware.

[OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist.
