Use the installed OpenSpec apply workflow/skill as the implementation procedure.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

1. Run:
   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

2. Run:
   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

3. Treat the returned OpenSpec state, instruction, tasks, context, operationGuidance, and contextFiles as authoritative.

4. Read all contextFiles relevant to the remaining work before modifying code.

Resume from the first genuinely incomplete task. Do not redo completed work unnecessarily.

Implement every remaining required task.

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".
- In the SAME turn where you legitimately flip an OpenSpec checkbox to "- [x]" (or otherwise complete that OpenSpec task), call complete_task with the corresponding GLLA id. One OpenSpec checkbox flip = one complete_task call. Never batch all syncs to the end of the session.
- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If the authoritative OpenSpec task set itself changes after attachment, do not silently ignore the difference or invent an independent plan. Reconcile against a fresh OpenSpec apply response before completion.

Run relevant builds, focused tests, integration tests, and regression checks as work progresses. Fix failures caused by this change rather than bypassing them.

Do not weaken, delete, rewrite, reinterpret, or silently defer OpenSpec requirements merely to make implementation easier.

Do not switch to a different OpenSpec change.

If OpenSpec reports state="blocked", resolve the missing required planning artifact through the OpenSpec workflow before continuing implementation. Do not invent missing requirements merely to get past the block.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

Before claiming completion, independently re-read:

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;
- the repository diff and working-tree state;
- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

Done when:

1. "openspec instructions apply --change add-touch-navigation --json" reports zero remaining required implementation tasks.

At the start of work, after every context compaction, after every resume, and whenever task state is uncertain:

   openspec status --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

   openspec instructions apply --change "add-touch-navigation" --json

GLLA task-list synchronization is a hard, per-task requirement, using GLLA's own task tools (not prose):

- GLLA task id N mirrors exactly one OpenSpec task; its title prefix "[OpenSpec <task-id>]" names that OpenSpec task.
- When you START a mirrored OpenSpec task, call update_task_status with that GLLA id and status "in_progress".

- When several mirrored tasks genuinely finish in one turn, one update_task_batch call is also acceptable.
- GLLA's pending-task gate REFUSES complete_goal while any mirrored GLLA task is still open — a stale mirror blocks goal completion even when OpenSpec itself is finished.
- Never mark either side complete merely because work was attempted.
- The bridge extension also mirrors OpenSpec completions into the GLLA list at turn boundaries as a safety net, but do not rely on it; keep the mirror correct yourself.

If OpenSpec reports state="all_done", do not immediately declare success. Perform the final verification below first.

- the current OpenSpec status;
- the current OpenSpec apply instructions;
- all relevant OpenSpec artifacts;

- the actual build/test/regression outputs.

[OpenSpec 16] 5.3 Discriminate the P52 pinch-zoom failure on-device (one scripted pass, no rebuild), then fix per the hypothesis the evidence selects. The per-finger-grouping hypothesis is REFUTED against Qt 6.6 primary sources and must not be re-investigated: the WM_POINTER handler aggregates every live finger into each delivery (qwindowspointerhandler.cpp re-appends non-delivered live points as Stationary) and fromNativeTouchPoints derives TouchBegin only when ALL points are Pressed, so finger 2 arrives as TouchUpdate [f2 Pressed, f1 Stationary], which TouchState promotes correctly. Ranked causes: (1) the tested binary predates the touch pipeline (Qt's default primary-finger-only mouse synthesis explains working one-finger rotate alone); (2) finger 1 crosses the ~10 logical-px slop while aiming finger 2 → STROKE → finger 2 blacklisted as second-class (rotate continues, zoom never); (3) the digitizer's first frame for finger 2 lacks POINTER_FLAG_DOWN and Qt drops the point ("ignore bogus updates"), so a second point is never observed; (4) QEvent::TouchCancel mid-gesture (touchEvent currently treats cancel as Update). Decode rubric: point count never exceeds 1 → cause 3 (or 1, ruled out by step 0); count reaches 2 and pinch still fails → cause 2 or 4 (escalate with an env-gated trace inside touchEvent); CANCELED flags / capture-changed frames → cause 4 (OS palm-suppression channel). — Verify: the trace and the selected hypothesis are recorded in this change; the fix lands via /opsx-apply (a slop/STROKE-promotion policy decision amends D2; a digitizer-level cause is filed as a follow-up change, not silently accepted); 5.2 pinch/pan re-recorded on the P52, passing regardless of the active tool. — **Discriminated (device evidence, no trace needed)**: the fresh P52 report (run 42630304893 installer, P0-fixed binary) shows the symptom **draws an atom immediately** with the draw tool active — the press demonstrably reaches the tool, so cause (1) is ruled out, and the symptom is exactly cause (2) (finger 1 crosses slop → STROKE → press → draw tool creates an atom; finger 2 arrives and is blacklisted → no zoom). [OpenSpec 17] 5.4 Touch pipeline correctness fixes that are evidence-backed independently of the 5.3 outcome (code changes via /opsx-apply): (a) coordinate space — TouchState consumes scenePosition(), which in Qt 6 widget delivery equals globalPosition() (qguiapplication.cpp sets scenePosition = globalPosition; QApplicationPrivate::updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal, never scenePosition), so on the real app layout every synthesized tap/lasso position is offset by the widget's GLOBAL origin (toolbar/dock chrome plus the window's on-screen position); the unit tests missed it because the fixture widget is top-level and a (0,0)-positioned parent makes mapTo(window) coincide with mapToGlobal. Correct at the GLWidget::touchEvent dispatch boundary by subtracting this->mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)) from each synthesized position (NOT in posOf(): QEventPoint::position() is unsettable on constructed points because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only in qeventpoint_p.h and absent on the Linux CI build, so reading position() in posOf() would break every state-machine test; the machine's internal math is translation-invariant, so global is safe internally). Pin with a touchnavigationtest fixture that embeds GLWidget as a child of a parent widget AND moves the parent to a non-zero global position so the test discriminates mapToGlobal from mapTo(window). (b) QEvent::TouchCancel — handle explicitly: PENDING → Idle with no events (today a cancel synthesizes a phantom click); STROKE → emit the synthesized release so the tool's stroke ends cleanly, then Idle; GESTURE → Idle holding the camera; clear the blacklist. (c) onBegin delivery-independence hardening — a single-point begin during PENDING must promote to GESTURE (at minimum it must not orphan the tracked finger); keep the per-finger-begin touchnavigationtest slot. — Verify: new/updated test slots pass under xvfb; full ctest suite stays green. — **Verified**: touchnavigationtest = 22 passed / 1 skipped (dpr), full ctest = 49/49 passed; the boundary-correction mechanism (mapToGlobal, over position()-in-posOf() because QMutableEventPoint is private-header-only) was validated against Qt 6.4.2 primary sources — scenePosition() == globalPosition(), and updateTouchPointsForWidget rewrites only position() = mapFromGlobal — and the discriminating test (parent moved to a non-zero global position) fails on the old mapTo(window) offset and passes on mapToGlobal.
